objective: Close the final v0.3.2 full-function evidence gap by proving that the OpenCode Go provider credential configured inside the Crew-owned DeepSeek Harness is usable by DSH Crew for a real worker, real explicit reviewer, and real automatic worker-to-reviewer pipeline. The Harness is the provider/credential authority; Crew must consume the Harness catalog/route and must not depend on OpenCode CLI login state or ad-hoc environment-key injection. Leave the machine installed and restore any temporary Crew routing changes exactly.
context: The user has now configured OpenCode Go inside the DeepSeek Harness running under the Crew-owned DSH_HOME (~/.config/dsh-crew/harness). Prior gates already proved: v0.3.2 candidate identity, complete install/uninstall/reinstall lifecycle, 449/449 deterministic tests, package/install/cohort gates, Hub/MCP/config/routing/job-control surfaces, OpenCode Go direct CLI inference, cancellation cleanup, and release-safety provenance. The only remaining gap was that the prior live gate used a Harness opencode-go route before the Harness itself had a provider credential, causing credential-resolution failure. This task must test the corrected architecture: Harness owns provider catalog + credential, Crew reads/selects Harness provider/model and dispatches through it. Current main before queueing is f5a341de679778165efa1ee8f224da06985c7c86; issue #45 remains open until this final live gate passes.
forbidden_changes: Any product source, test, package, README, CHANGELOG, lockfile, workflow, or validator change
Any npm publish, dist-tag, deprecate, unpublish, owner/token mutation, Git tag, GitHub Release, branch rewrite, merge, rebase, cherry-pick, or force-push
Any install, uninstall, purge, update, or reconfiguration of Crew, DSH, OpenCode, Codex, or Claude
Any read, copy, hash, print, export, or direct inspection of Harness credential files/stores, OpenCode auth.json, API keys, tokens, cookies, OTPs, auth headers, or secret values
Any ad-hoc OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY, OPENCODE_ALT_API_KEY, or other provider-key environment injection used to bypass the Harness credential store
Any access to the user's official ~/.dsh home, official web profile, or official DSH credentials
Any permanent mutation of ~/.config/dsh-crew/config.json or other long-lived Crew settings
Any provider fallback to an unrelated route without explicit trace evidence
Any host/main-agent substitution for a failed delegated worker/reviewer execution
validation: Checkout main and git pull --ff-only. Resolve source_commit LATEST to the actual HEAD, require a clean repository, and run `node .agent-workflow/validator/validate-contract.mjs task docs/agent-tasks/ACTIVE_TASK.json`; this task contract itself must PASS validation before proceeding. Require package.json and runtime identity to be 0.3.2 and `node scripts/setup.mjs status` to report DSH plugin, Codex Desktop integration, and Claude Code integration installed.

Use only the Crew-owned Harness: DSH_HOME must resolve to ~/.config/dsh-crew/harness and profile dsh-crew. Do not touch official ~/.dsh. Through sanctioned Harness/Crew APIs or CLI surfaces, confirm the Harness model catalog includes provider opencode-go with deepseek-v4-flash and deepseek-v4-pro and that the provider is credential-ready. Record only provider/model identities and redacted readiness state; never inspect credential contents or credential-store files. Do not treat OpenCode CLI auth as the credential source for this gate.

Before any Crew routing mutation, snapshot ~/.config/dsh-crew/config.json exact bytes (or absence) in a disposable temp location and record only byte count + SHA-256 digest. Any temporary routing override must be restored byte-for-byte in a finally/cleanup path. Do not record unrelated config values.

If needed, temporarily set Crew worker/reviewer model priorities through Crew's own config writer/API so flash resolves to opencode-go/deepseek-v4-flash and pro/reviewer resolves to opencode-go/deepseek-v4-pro, while preserving Harness as provider/credential authority. Start a bounded live Crew Hub using the Crew-owned DSH_HOME/profile and require provider/model endpoints to show the intended opencode-go flash/pro selections before dispatch.

Create a disposable git repository under the OS temp directory. Through the real MCP stdio server / live Hub path, run a blocking real worker on a tiny deterministic coding task. Require actual model execution success through Harness using provider=opencode-go and model=deepseek-v4-flash (or exact catalog-equivalent flash id), verified delivery/candidate evidence, isolated worktree evidence, primary workspace safety, and no silent host fallback. A route-selection-only or credential-readiness-only result is insufficient.

On the completed candidate, run a real explicit reviewer through the live Crew path. Require actual model execution success through Harness using provider=opencode-go and model=deepseek-v4-pro (or exact catalog-equivalent pro id), review-only behavior, structured findings/evidence/risks/verdict, and no unauthorized candidate modification. A manually fabricated review or pre-dispatch success is insufficient.

Run a second tiny workflow with automatic review enabled using the current canonical review-pipeline control. Require the same workflow to execute a real opencode-go flash worker followed automatically by a real opencode-go pro reviewer, with child-attempt/selection trace, terminal verified outcome, and structured review. The explicit reviewer from the previous step does not count for this criterion.

Verify cleanup truthfulness for every worktree created by this task: no task-created worktree remains registered in git worktree list and no task-created worktree directory remains on disk after successful/failed/cancelled completion. If any persistent cleanup failure exists, require workspace_retained=true plus cleanup_warning and return BLOCKED/FAIL rather than claiming PASS.

In a finally/cleanup phase, stop all Hub/MCP test processes and free acceptance ports; remove disposable repositories/worktrees; restore ~/.config/dsh-crew/config.json byte-for-byte to the pre-test snapshot (or restore absence), re-hash, and require exact digest equality. Run `node scripts/setup.mjs status` again and require DSH plugin + Codex + Claude installed. final_machine_state must be INSTALLED.

Run `git diff --check`. The repository must be clean except the Result Contract while drafting. Write schema-v2 Result Contract to docs/agent-results/TASK-V032-HARNESS-PROVIDER-FINAL-ACCEPTANCE-result.json with exact live provider/model evidence, worker/reviewer/auto-review evidence, cleanup evidence, config restore digest equality, final_machine_state, and blockers. Run the result validator with --stamp, delete ACTIVE_TASK, commit/push only the Result + ACTIVE_TASK deletion, then stop.
acceptance_criteria: Harness itself, under the Crew-owned DSH_HOME, is the proven provider/credential authority for opencode-go; no direct credential-store read and no ad-hoc provider-key environment injection is used.
A real Crew worker executes successfully through Harness using OpenCode Go flash with verified delivery and isolated workspace evidence.
A real explicit Crew reviewer executes successfully through Harness using OpenCode Go pro and remains review-only.
A real automatic worker-to-reviewer pipeline executes both agents successfully in one workflow with OpenCode Go flash then pro and terminates with verified review evidence.
Every task-created worktree is actually removed, the user's Crew config is restored byte-for-byte, no official DSH state or secret values are touched, and final_machine_state is INSTALLED.

Full success requires Result status PASS, all Result tests PASS, result_validation.status PASS, and summary containing exactly `FULL_FUNCTION_ACCEPTANCE: PASS` and `final_machine_state: INSTALLED`. Any inability to execute the worker, reviewer, automatic review, exact config restoration, or cleanup must return BLOCKED/FAIL with precise evidence.
